title: Target trial framework for determining the effect of changes in training load on injury risk using observational data: a methodological commentary
authors: Wang C, Kaufman JS, Steele RJ, Shrier I
population: Methodological commentary on load-and-injury studies in sport; no participants
findings: States that conventional methods used to study the relationship between load and injury are prone to bias.
Describes the target trial framework: emulate a hypothetical randomised trial using observational data, with explicitly defined research questions and study design, to estimate causal effects.
Gives an overview of the framework's components as applied to load and injury studies and the design and analysis considerations needed to minimise bias.
No empirical result or threshold is reported.
limitations: Commentary with no data, so it supplies no threshold. It shows how a progression-rule effect could be estimated, not that any such analysis exists for running.
implications: Treat every progression threshold in the corpus as an association from observational data, not a causal limit; copy and ADR text should not say that exceeding the limit causes injury.

The route to testing a spike or ramp rule without a randomised trial is a target trial emulation on session-level data; logging planned versus actual load in the app would make such an analysis possible later (a design suggestion, not stated in the paper).

verification.notes: Re-fetched Crossref (first author Wang, 4 authors, 2024-07) and Europe PMC abstract (PMID 38975026). Findings match; 'prone to bias' stated as in the abstract.
